snapshot.scope: Independent Product Planning review of the B6.05 single pinned local embedding asset interface: strict CAS lifecycle, private verified atomic install/recovery, lexical fallback and no B6.06 runtime or provider claims.

reviewers.independence: Product Planning reviewed API, Settings, UI, architecture, dependency and trace owners against the strict interface checkpoint; Development and UI independently own the later asset service and visual implementation.

dimensions.summary: Local Capabilities exposes one asset and applicable Install, Enable, Disable or Remove without provider or path complexity.
API, Settings, UI, architecture and dependency owners agree on revision CAS, exact pin, atomic lifecycle and lexical fallback.
PIGE-SEARCH-003 and E6.02 remain partial while B6.05 implementation, B6.06 runtime and packaged evidence remain open.
Canonical schemas, preload channels and dependency identity give Development and UI one bounded interface.
Existing owners bind the slice without a new provider surface, model manifest or broad RAG framework.

verification.evidence: Lifecycle schemas and exact preload channel projection are strict and path/provider-free.

verification.command: npm run verify:docs && npm run verify:decisions && npm run verify:dependencies
verification.evidence: API, Settings, UI, architecture, Decision and exact dependency pin agree.
Partial Search/RAG acceptance remains synchronized with B6.05-only scope.

coordination.compatibility: Existing lexical search remains available; the new interface adds one optional machine asset without changing search modes or provider settings.
coordination.acknowledgement: Planning binds B6.05 asset lifecycle only; service/UI implementation, B6.06 vector runtime/index integration and packaged acceptance stay open.

nonBlockingRisks: Real download, interruption, recovery, enable/disable/remove and platform evidence remain acceptance work.
The GGUF inference runtime, vectors and semantic ranking remain B6.06 work.
A future pin change requires reviewed dependency identity and derived-index rebuild evidence.
